Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Make the six failing queries run on 1 CN (fusion, spill, or both). Findings to read: P1, B1, B2, P5 (RIGHT_SEMI gap). Code to read: compute_node_service.rs process_fragment/translate path and local_exchange register_receiver at the TPlan level; ExchangeNode row layout guarantees; translator join lowering; streaming_fragment.cpp output repositories; downgrade_executor tiers; sirius_ffi.cpp output_row_count/export_packed HOST-tier; which of the six each option rescues and at what cost.
Angle: the design a senior engineer would ship for the long run: correct under cancellation and concurrency, observable (log/telemetry), configurable where it must be, with the failure modes enumerated.
Produce ONE complete design: mechanism (what changes, in which functions, how it behaves under the measured SF1000 case and under the 15 passing queries), files to touch, tests (unit/component and the SF1000 acceptance), predicted effect with numbers derived from the evidence, risks, effort, dependencies on the other three fixes. Write your full design as markdown to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-robust.md (include the code excerpts you relied on with file:line) and return the structured summary.

Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.

Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.
- dataset-manager: Use this skill to generate benchmark datasets (TPC-H, TPC-DS, etc.). Trigger when the user needs test data at a specific scale factor for benchmarking or testing. Supports parquet and duckdb output formats.
- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).
- module-context: Automatically identify which dependency library modules are relevant to a task and load their API documentation into context. Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.
- profile-analyzer: Use this skill to understand why a Sirius query is slow, identify GPU bottlenecks, or detect performance regressions. Generates reports with kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, operator attribution, and cross-run comparisons. 1	# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
4	(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
5	Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
6	one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
7	Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.
8	
9	## The four issues
10	
11	| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
14	| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
15	| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
16	| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |
17	
18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.
24	
25	## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)
26	
27	1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
28	2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
29	3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
30	4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
31	5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.
32	
33	## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")
34	
35	| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
38	| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
39	| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
40	| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |
41	
42	## Workflows
43	
44	**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.
45	
46	**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)

- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## 3. Findings by dimension

Notation: **P** planning, **C** cardinality, **B** backpressure. Confirmed findings first in each dimension (both a data skeptic and a source skeptic failed to refute them; their corrections are folded in), then disputed findings with the objection stated, then lower-ranked findings that were not adversarially verified (marked as such).

### 3A. Planning

#### P1 (confirmed). The six 1-CN failures are one FE plan shape: an unfiltered lineitem leaf feeding a hash-partitioned exchange, whose whole output must be parked on the GPU

**Measured.** In all six plans the failing fragment is a bare lineitem `FileScanNode` under a `HASH_PARTITIONED` `TDataStreamSink` with one destination (survey/plan-summary.txt lines 10, 16, 18, 34, 36, 42; dumps cn1/dump/fragment-0141 (q05, node 8), 0208 (q08), 0220 (q09), 0427 (q17, node 0), 0437 (q18, node 9), 0504 (q21, node 12), each `output_partition TPartitionType(2)` = HASH_PARTITIONED per `Partitions.thrift:41-49`). The FE join labels differ (q05/q08/q09/q17 PARTITIONED, q18 `11:INNER JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`, q21 `14:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`), the sink type does not. Lineitem is the build-side exchange in five plans and the probe-side exchange in q17. Every one of the six failing fragments was started as `role=sender inputs=0 outputs=1` (cn1/cluster.log lines 4200, 7854, 9840, 16770, 18095, 20282).

3:This document covers the memory tier hierarchy, reservation system, downgrade executor, and pinned host memory management.
5:## Memory Tier Hierarchy
11:│  GPU Memory (Tier 0)     │  Fast, limited (~24GB typical)
14:│  Host Pinned (Tier 1)    │  Medium speed, larger (>100GB)
17:│  Disk (Tier 2)           │  Slow, unlimited (~1TB default)

49:downgrade_trigger_fraction = 0.8;

57:downgrade_trigger_fraction = 0.9;

93:**File:** `src/include/downgrade/downgrade_executor.hpp`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp`
95:One `downgrade_executor` per memory space monitors pressure and moves data to lower tiers.
99:- **Processing thread**: dequeues `downgrade_request` objects sequentially from an `interruptible_mpmc` queue
100:- **Monitor thread** (if `monitor_period > 0`): each cycle, if the memory space reports `should_downgrade_memory()`, it applies a **stateless viability gate** (`has_viable_downgrade_target()`) before enqueuing. A request is only fired when a lower tier could plausibly accept the data:
102:  - Without DISK, only a GPU source has a lower tier (HOST). Viability is confirmed by probing each HOST space with a chunk-sized `make_reservation_or_null` (released immediately) — the ground truth for whether downgraded data can actually land, since HOST capacity reflects both live reservations and already-stored downgraded data.
108:The monitor is not on the correctness-critical path: the pipeline executor drives downgrade on demand via `request_downgrade()` independently, so monitor back-off can never wedge a query. Monitor-issued requests are fire-and-forget.
112:The downgrade executor uses a request-based model with tiered candidate fetching:
114:1. Caller invokes `request_downgrade(predicate)` which constructs a `downgrade_request` and pushes it onto the MPMC queue. Returns `std::future<size_t>`.
117:   - **Tier 1 (data repositories):** Creates a `convertible_data_batch_provider` per repository and fetches idle GPU-resident batches one at a time
118:   - **Tier 2 (task_scheduler queue):** Creates a `convertible_gpu_pipeline_task_provider` to extract tasks with convertible data batches from the pipeline-level task queue
121:**Pipeline integration:** When `gpu_pipeline_executor` gets a partial memory reservation (shortfall), it issues a single `request_downgrade(predicate)` where the predicate attempts `make_reservation_or_null(bytes_needed)`. The downgrade stops as soon as the reservation succeeds -- single request, no over-freeing.
127:1. **Data repositories** are iterated in repository manager order. Within each repository, `convertible_data_batch_provider` iterates partitions back-to-front, then batches back-to-front, filtering for idle batches in the source memory space.

Confirmed findings first in each dimension (both a data skeptic and a source skeptic failed to refute them; their corrections are folded in), then disputed findings with the objection stated, then lower-ranked findings that were not adversarially verified (marked as such).
4	
5	### 3A. Planning
6	
7	#### P1 (confirmed). The six 1-CN failures are one FE plan shape: an unfiltered lineitem leaf feeding a hash-partitioned exchange, whose whole output must be parked on the GPU
8	
9	**Measured.** In all six plans the failing fragment is a bare lineitem `FileScanNode` under a `HASH_PARTITIONED` `TDataStreamSink` with one destination (survey/plan-summary.txt lines 10, 16, 18, 34, 36, 42; dumps cn1/dump/fragment-0141 (q05, node 8), 0208 (q08), 0220 (q09), 0427 (q17, node 0), 0437 (q18, node 9), 0504 (q21, node 12), each `output_partition TPartitionType(2)` = HASH_PARTITIONED per `Partitions.thrift:41-49`). The FE join labels differ (q05/q08/q09/q17 PARTITIONED, q18 `11:INNER JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`, q21 `14:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`), the sink type does not. Lineitem is the build-side exchange in five plans and the probe-side exchange in q17. Every one of the six failing fragments was started as `role=sender inputs=0 outputs=1` (cn1/cluster.log lines 4200, 7854, 9840, 16770, 18095, 20282).

On 4 CNs the planner logs `Not wiring dynamic filter(s): build side carries neither filter nor opaque-build evidence` (cn4/engine-.cn1.log 13:19:58.309). ~1.0 s of GPU operator time, ~0.25-0.3 s of wall in the join fragment. Proposed: treat a declared stream far below the base table as filter evidence (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664`) and add a dependency edge from the DF pipeline to the build's publish when the probe is a parked stream. Medium confidence.
109	- **The engine's in-fragment re-plan works, but only inside a fragment (PC-6).** Declared stream cardinalities equal actual parked rows for every stream (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare), DuckDB reorders inner joins with them (q19: engine built on filtered part and probed the 128.6M-row lineitem stream, cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546; q07: build/probe of three joins flipped vs the FE), but `STATISTICS_PROPAGATION` is disabled (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240`), so a FILES() scan inside the same fragment keeps its raw estimate, and the fragment cut is fixed before any of this. Also see C2.
110	- **Two-phase aggregation is cheap (AGG-5).** q01/q06 merge and result fragments 3-24 ms, hops 1-7 ms, 20-40 ms total post-scan; parity 1.04/0.97. The translator's decimal lowering shifts ~0.5 s of summed GPU time into PROJECTION and is the 9.6e-4 deviation source. Low priority.
111	
112	#### Disputed planning finding
113	
114	**PC-3: "the 4-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip is the measured source of the 0.43-0.59 scaling efficiency": refuted on the causal claim, plan facts stand.** The data skeptic's objection: the efficiency band exists without any data movement. q01 moves 0.00 GB and reaches 0.59; q06 0.00 GB, 0.56; q15 1.27 GB, 0.58; q19 2.75 GB, 0.53; against q03 60.34 GB, 0.48 and q07 69.01 GB, 0.43 (results-ratios.md, cn4-transmits.txt). Movement therefore accounts for at most ~0.05-0.15 of efficiency on the heaviest queries and none of the ~0.4 baseline loss. The baseline loss is measured elsewhere: per-GB `GPU_SCAN` Computing rises 1.3-1.6x on 4 CNs for every query including the join-free ones (q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q14 0.069 -> 0.112; cn1-quent.json vs cn4-quent.json top_ops), and ~0.2 s per query is outside the engine span on both arms (P4). Two attributions in PC-3 are also wrong: q07's dominant mover is the 1.82B-row lineitem shuffle (43.75 GB), not the 600M-row customer broadcast (3.71 GB); q02's are the four 800M-row partsupp shuffles (38.5 GB), not the 472M-row broadcast (4.25 GB). q12's orders shuffle is off the critical path (sender Computing 0.255 s overlapping the compute-bound lineitem scan). Keep the table in P3 as the plan-level fact; do not attribute the efficiency band to it.
115	
116	### 3B. Cardinality
117	
118	#### C1 (confirmed). Every FE estimate is 1 row; actuals reach 6.0e9
119	
120	**Measured.** `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (survey/plan-summary.txt). Exchanges carrying >= 100M rows on 1 CN (card-compare-cn1.txt, last line): q02/exch3 800M, q02/exch28 800M, q02/exch34 118M, q02/exch36 118M, q03/exch8 146M, q04/exch4 3,793M, q05/exch1 150M, q05/exch4 228M, q07/exch8 1,823M, q07/exch12 1,500M, q07/exch16 150M, q10/exch12 115M, q13/exch2 1,484M, q13/exch4 150M, q14/exch3 200M, q19/exch3 129M, q20/exch9 304M, q20/exch12 800M, q21/exch6 731M, q22/exch10 1,500M. On 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt) the list grows to 26 entries and the summed broadcast rows reach 6,000M (q22/exch10).
121	
122	**Source.** `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676` (quoted in P1). Reached for FILES() via `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (:374-375). Consequences confirmed in source: `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` inert (P3); CTE inlining always wins (P5); `JoinCommutativityRule` never commutes semi/anti (P5); the translator comment at `node_translator.rs:1918-1929` already records that "the FE reports cardinality: 1 for every FILES() external scan" and that "bounding it belongs to the executor".
123	
124	**Where row counts already exist.** (a) FE-only, no wire change: `TableFunctionTable.parseFilesForLoadAndQuery` records every file's byte size (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java:611 brokerFileStatus.setSize(fileStatus.getLen())`, exposed via `loadFileList()` :300); `computeFileScanNode` can estimate rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema. (b) Exact: `file_schema.rs:19-27` already opens every footer (`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder` metadata) for the schema RPC; `FileMetaData.num_rows` is available but `PGetFileSchemaResult` carries only status + schema (`gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:647-650`), so this is a proto + FE + CN change, not FE-only. (c) Later: per-column min/max from row-group stats for the date range predicates.
125	
126	**Limits (inference, from the FE estimator code).** Row counts without column statistics leave `ColumnStatistic.unknown()` in place: range predicates on unknown columns cost 0.5 (`BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.estimatePredicateRange` -> `OVERLAP_INFINITE_RANGE_FILTER_COEFFICIENT`), IN 0.5, string equality 1.0, and join output = `max(L, R)` (`StatisticsCalculator.computeJoinNode :1219-1240`). That separates lineitem from nation and orders from region, which is what the fragment cut needs most, but it also arms the broadcast guard against mid-sized broadcasts (P3) and gives no NDV for the aggregate outputs that decide q02's join 37. Verify with `EXPLAIN COSTS` on q05/q22/q03 after the change; this was not run.
127	
128	Confidence: high on the defect; medium-high on fix (a); the predicted plan outcomes are inference.
129	
130	#### C2 (confirmed). The receiver-first exact cardinality mechanism is correct but arrives too late and is undermined by a flat 0.2 selectivity on the FE's `IS NOT NULL` conjunct
131	
132	**Measured.** `engine.rs:551-590` sums parked `output_row_count` over local senders and remote batch rows and calls `declare_input_cardinality` before `build()`; `src/include/exec/stream_bind_catalog.hpp:42-47` feeds it to DuckDB's TableFunction cardinality callback. Every declared count equals the actual parked rows (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare-cn1.txt). It only helps inside a fragment: q19's engine plan builds on the filtered part and probes the stream (cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546: `STREAMING_SOURCE(4)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(5)` 3.66 GB -> 0.01 GB, fragment 150 ms) although the FE made lineitem the build.
133	
134	**BJ-4 (not adversarially verified, medium confidence).** In q10 the receiver builds on the 150M-row, 25.5 GB customer x nation side instead of the 114.7M-row, 2.29 GB stream (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573: `PARTITION(8) 25.55 GB 0.479 s, CONCAT(9) 0.114 s, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.301 s`; the stream is behind `DYNAMIC_FILTER(11)`, i.e. probe). The translated plan carries `Filter[is_not_null($0)](customer Read)` from the FE's null-rejecting scan conjunct (`expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`), and DuckDB applies `DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2` to it (`duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57`), so 150M x 0.2 = 30M < 114.7M declared. Standalone has no such filter and estimates customer x nation at 151.5M. The 0.2 arithmetic is inferred from source, not from a printed estimate. Proposed (translator, `experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src/expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`; medium confidence): do not emit the FE's join-key `IS NOT NULL` conjunct as a Filter rel (the join drops nulls anyway), or attach it to the ReadRel as a table filter. Measured stake: the `PARTITION(8) + CONCAT(9) + HASH_JOIN(14)` chain is 0.89 s of summed GPU time in q10's 1067 ms receiver fragment (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573).
135	
136	#### C3 (confirmed, one correction). The engine's own reservation estimate is exact once a pipeline has history, but the cold-start estimate is 8x, and four cold-start scan tasks reserve 58-80% of the pool
137	
138	**Measured** (agent-notes/req_hist.py, raw Quent Reserving records). q01: after the first task completes, each scan task requests exactly its measured peak (6.98 GB for a 2.41 GB input, 2.9x); the first 4 tasks of every scan pipeline request 19.52 GB each (histogram `{8.1: 4, 2.9: 103}`). q06: 13.32 GB x 4 then 3.74 GB. Source: `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:66 kMaxNumericCarrierExpansion = 8`, `:648-668 no_history_peak_memory_estimate` = bytes x 8 + filter working set; `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:872-880` takes the no-history branch for every task dispatched before the first completion. Max concurrent reservation held by the 4 slots (agent-notes/bj6_sweep.py): q03 79.6 GiB, q10 75.9, q12 79.7, q14 67.7, q19 58.0 on cn1; the same per CN on cn4 and in standalone. Reservations are charged to the same counter as live allocations (`cucascade/src/memory/reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`), and the engine's `[gpu_pool]` running peak reached 99.16 GB (92%) inside q03.r0's lineitem fragment and 106.09 GB (98.8%) in q04.r0 (cn1/engine-cn0.log windows 51 and 65).
139	
140	Summed request vs summed peak (reservation-ratio.txt): cn1 q11 236.2 GB vs 4.3 GB (54x), q14 15.2x, q03 14.2x, q10 6.3x; cn4 q11 67.7x; standalone q13 549.8 GB vs 0.9 GB (611x, DENSE_COUNT_JOIN path), q14 68x. On 4 CNs every CN pays the 4-task wave per fragment, which is the whole of the higher 1.27/1.64 ratios for q01/q06.
141	
142	**Join/receiver fragments over-reserve through a different path (measured, mechanism not investigated).** The scan cold-start rule above does not explain the receiver fragments: cn1 q04.r1 F00 (orders scan + RIGHT_SEMI join over the 30.8 GB lineitem stream, 151 tasks) requested 253.1 GB for a 61.3 GB summed peak (4.1x; cn1-quent.txt q04.r1 fragment `...8480`), q07.r1 F08 (217 tasks, four joins) 163.1 GB for 26.3 GB (6.2x; fragment `...753ea`), q13.r1 F04 100.7 GB for 43.8 GB (2.3x). Reserving time in these fragments is 0.002-0.043 s, so the over-estimate did not block them at the 100 GiB pool; it would at a smaller pool or more slots. The operator-level estimates (hash join / partition / concat) were not read for this report; listed in section 5.
143	
144	**Correction to BJ-6.** The gate did trip at 1 CN: every Reserving > 10 ms in q10/q12/q14 ends exactly when another task releases (agent-notes/refute-bj6/slow_reserving.py: q10 r0/r1/r2 177.1/177.7/174.4 ms for a 20.4 GB request while 3 tasks held 61.1 GB plus 31.6 GB of leaked parked data, finding B4; q12 108.6 + 47.0 ms; q14 128-139 ms), reproducibly in all three runs, 0 at 4 CNs and in standalone. `memory_space::make_reservation` blocks on a notification channel until a release (`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`, `notification_channel.cpp:47-59`). Cost <= 0.18 s per query today.
145	
146	**q20 partial-aggregate growth (SAJ-6, measured).** exch 9 carries 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN and 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (2.1x) because each CN pre-aggregates a quarter of lineitem-1994 with fewer duplicates per group.
147	
148	**Proposed.** In `no_history_peak_memory_estimate` use the split's decoded column-buffer estimate (already computed for the history clamp, `docs/super-sirius/scan.md:42`) as the fresh-read basis, keeping 8x as fallback; or cap the no-history wave to a fraction of the space max. Verify with the Reserving histogram (first 4 requests ~7 GB) and 0 OOM reschedules. Confidence high on the mechanism; note that the documented `pipeline.num_threads 8` tuning (`configuration.md:788-800`) would make the first wave 8 x 19.5 = 156 GB of a 107 GB pool, which is the likely mechanism behind the documented 12-thread cliff (inference).
149	
150	### 3C. Backpressure
151	
152	#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation
153	
154	**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). Inside the engine, `Fragment::build()` opens a `StandaloneQueryScope` that takes the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`) until `run()` finishes, so two fragments cannot be in flight on one context even if the CN asked (source skeptic; this makes "run sender and receiver concurrently" engine work, not CN work).
155	
156	**Measured, q05 timeline.** All 11 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs arrived 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cn1/cluster.log 4142-4202). Fragments ran strictly sequentially: nation 6 ms, region 9 ms, then the lineitem sender 5774 started 13:03:43.434 with `allocated=2304 bytes` (engine-cn0.log:49203, an empty pool) and parked 39 batches x 2.668 GB = 104.06 GB by +1.315 s (Quent data_batch Stationary events: 26.7 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s); first OOM at +1.361 s (engine-cn0.log:49221 `requested 748875880 bytes ... global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864`). The supplier/customer/orders fragments started only after the failure at 13:05:24.632+ (cluster.log 6072-6305); the receiver of streams 7 and 9 never started (Quent shows 7 of 11 fragments). Receiver 5775 later ran in 73 ms and its output sat parked for 184.5 s until q08's failure wipe (cn1-quent.txt wall=184.502 s, Comp=0.128 s).
157	
158	**Measured, passing queries show the same shape under the cap.** cn1 q07.r0: all 7 senders finished before the join fragment started (cluster.log 6807-7005); 59.47 GB of lineitem plus 18.38 GB of orders were parked (79.1 GB, 74% of the pool) with dwell up to 2.76 s. cn4 q07.r1: every `fragment run finished` precedes its first `transmitted batches via nixl`. Per-fragment run sums vs span (MFS-4): cn1 q02.r1 13 fragments sum 977 ms, span 1067 ms, gaps 90 ms (8%); cn4 q02.r1 cn0 sum 748 ms, span 1081 ms, gaps 333 ms (31%), the largest before receivers waiting for the other CNs' senders. The 4-slot executor idles during the many 1-task fragments (cn1 q02.r1: 133 tasks, Comp 2.9 s in a 1.06 s span = 2.7 of 4 slots busy).
159	
160	**Streaming works within a fragment.** q21 fragment 2acb (ran after the failure) streamed a 123 GB lineitem scan through FILTER -> HASH_JOIN in 3.15 s with only 46.47 GB partitioned out (cn1-quent.txt q21.r0). Only the exchange forces full materialisation.
161	
162	**Proposed.** Two routes: (1) on 1 CN, fuse local-only fragments before translation (P1, item 2); every exchange is local, the fused plan is the standalone plan, no engine change. (2) Streaming receivers: build once build-side streams are complete, consume probe-side streams while the sender still runs, run sender and receiver concurrently. (2) requires per-fragment lifecycle/task creators in the engine (the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` and the shared `task_creator_` reset in `begin_execution_window`, `sirius_context.cpp:392-395`) and a build/probe decision before the streamed side's cardinality is known. Confidence high on the mechanism; medium (1) and low-medium (2) on design effort.
163	
164	#### B2 (confirmed, mechanism sharpened). Parked batches are invisible to the downgrade sweep, so every OOM cycle frees 0 bytes although a 160 GiB HOST tier is configured
165	
166	**Measured.** cn1/engine-cn0.log: 17,917 lines `[downgrade] [GPU:0] downgrade request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured; data cannot be spilled to disk` and 17,917 `after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (...) -- proceeding with partial reservation`; per query 2503/3603/5603/2103/2302/1803. Zero lines with non-zero bytes freed. `[host_pool] HOST:0 ... allocated=72351744` is constant through the q05 storm (the host tier exists: `HOST_MEM=160GiB` -> `sirius.memory.host.capacity_bytes`, `engine_settings.rs:111-116`; `1 host memory space(s) created`). The bench kit already documents "host spill is NOT implemented" (`benchmarks/tpch/run-abc.sh:1038`).
167	
168	**Source (verified).** `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`: `// Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment.` `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()` (and `_input_repos` likewise). The only registration path into a per-query manager is `repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-71 add_new_repository` (inter-pipeline ports). `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232` TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers only; `:294-300` TIER 2 the pipeline task queue (queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches). The warning at `:357-363` fires whenever no DISK tier exists and the request is unsatisfied, regardless of whether any candidate existed. `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch (the CN swallows it with `.ok()` and plans blind, engine.rs:564, 582-585); `:822-825 export_packed` throws too, which would fail the 4-CN path on a spilled batch.
169	
170	**Correction.** The original clause "the sender's engine query has already ended" is not the operative reason. In q05/q08/q09 the bytes that filled the pool (104.30/99.54/96.42 GB) are the *running* leaf fragment's own STREAMING_SINK output; its query and manager existed, but a `GPU_SCAN -> STREAMING_SINK` fragment registers no repository at all. Finished-sender outputs account for 0 / 4.7 / 8.8 GB in those three, 38.2 / 68.7 / 77.8 GB in q17/q18/q21. The escape from the manager is the whole mechanism, and the receiver's `_input_repos` are equally invisible.
171	
172	**Impact arithmetic (inference).** Spilled data has to fit GPU + HOST = 107.4 + 171.8 = 279 GB. Totals a working spill would have to hold: q17 ~160 GB, q18 ~166, q05 ~171, q21 ~195, q08 ~200, q09 ~253. Five of six would plausibly pass slowly; q09 is marginal after the 16 GiB staging arena and the ~34 GB host-pool peak. The original "host spill rescues only q17/q18" compared against the host tier alone and should be dropped.
173	
174	**Proposed.** Register the streaming sink's output repositories and the receiver's input repositories with a process-level registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, including the running fragment's own sink (otherwise q05/q08/q09 still die). Make `Fragment::output_row_count` read a row count from host metadata and `export_packed` accept HOST-tier batches (the local relay already upgrades HOST -> GPU in `lock_or_prepare_batch`). Correct the warning to distinguish "no convertible candidates" from "no disk tier". Note the newest-first fairness policy at `downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216`; the candidate that matters here is the newest fragment's own output. Confidence high on the mechanism, medium that spill is worth doing before P1/B1.
175	
176	#### B3 (confirmed). The reschedule loop has no feasibility check: 179 stuck scan tasks x 100 retries x 50 ms, re-reading the split each time, while nothing can free memory
177	
178	**Source (verified).** `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348 static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;` (comment: bumped from 10 for cross-GPU batch-lock contention), `:409 sleep_for(50ms)`, termination only by count (`:349-364`) or `_completion_handler->has_error()` (`:314`); `:263` proceeds with a partial reservation after 0 bytes freed. Each retry resumes at operator index 0 and re-runs `materialize_table` for the same split (`sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:530-533, 592-593`). No knob: `exec/config.hpp` has no retry field.
179	
180	**Measured** (agent-notes/skeptic-oom4/retry_stats.py over cn1/engine-cn0.log):
181	
182	| query | stuck tasks | reschedules | first OOM (from client start) | last reschedule | wall to die (s) |
183	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
184	| q05 | 25 | 2500 | +1.61 s | +101.33 s | 101.5 |
185	| q08 | 36 | 3600 | +1.73 | +168.15 | 168.3 |
186	| q09 | 56 | 5600 | +2.38 | +232.41 | 232.5 |
187	| q17 | 21 | 2100 | +1.20 | +103.74 | 103.9 |

28	    /// Substrait relation built for the StarRocks subtree.
29	    pub rel: Rel,
30	    /// Tuple ids visible in the relation output row.
31	    ///
32	    /// For multi-input relations (joins, set ops) this is the left-to-right
33	    /// concatenation of the child layouts, so `DescriptorTable::slot_global_index`
34	    /// resolves a right-side slot to `left_width + right_index`. New multi-input
35	    /// translators MUST follow this ordering.
36	    pub row_tuples: Vec<i32>,
37	    /// Number of columns this relation emits.
38	    ///
39	    /// Carried as an invariant (rather than recomputed by walking `rel`) so a
40	    /// parent projection can compute its `output_mapping` base offset without
41	    /// teaching a column-counting helper about every relation type — a pattern
42	    /// that silently produced a wrong offset the moment an unknown relation
43	    /// appeared mid-tree. Every relation built here MUST set its true width.
44	    pub output_width: usize,
45	    /// Common-expr columns carried past the descriptor row (see [`translate_project_node`]).
46	    ///
47	    /// Invariant: columns `[0, output_width - carried_slots.len())` are exactly the
48	    /// concatenation of `materialized_slot_ids(t)` for `t` in `row_tuples`; the carried
49	    /// columns occupy the tail `[output_width - carried_slots.len(), output_width)`.
50	    /// Deliberately no `Default` impl: every construction site must decide whether carried
51	    /// columns survive it — width-preserving nodes pass them through, re-materializing nodes
52	    /// drop them by construction, joins refuse them, and the fragment root narrows them away.
53	    pub carried_slots: Vec<CarriedSlot>,
54	}
55	
56	/// Mutable state shared by plan-node translators.
57	struct PlanContext<'a> {
58	    /// Descriptor lookups for row layouts, tables, and scan schemas.
59	    desc: &'a DescriptorTable,
60	    /// Parquet file paths for each scan node, collected from the fragment's broker
61	    /// scan ranges. Scans with paths emit a `local_files` read; path-less scans
62	    /// fall back to a named-table read.
63	    scan_paths: &'a ScanFilePaths,
64	    /// Same-node input streams keyed by receiver exchange node id.
65	    exchange_inputs: &'a std::collections::HashMap<i32, &'a ExchangeInput>,
66	    /// Substrait extension registry shared across the whole plan.
67	    registry: &'a mut ExtensionRegistry,
68	    /// Schema of every exchange lowered to a stream read, in translation order. The caller has to
69	    /// declare these on the engine before the plan can bind.
70	    stream_inputs: Vec<StreamInputSchema>,
71	    /// Positional wire-column overrides, keyed by exchange node id, for exchanges that feed
72	    /// merge aggregations: the FE declares those columns with intermediate slot types that lie
73	    /// about what the sender ships, and allocates one slot for a state that can be wider (see
74	    /// `partial_state`). Computed by [`merge_exchange_overrides`] before translation starts.
75	    exchange_state_overrides: std::collections::HashMap<i32, Vec<StateColumns>>,
76	    /// Set when a partial aggregation emitted more columns than its FE output tuple declares.
77	    /// The fragment's root output names come from here instead of the descriptor table.
78	    partial_expansion: Option<PartialExpansion>,
79	    /// Common-expr slots each project must physically carry because an ancestor consumes them,
80	    /// keyed by project node id with slot ids ascending. Computed by
81	    /// [`common_slots_consumed_above`] before translation starts.
82	    consumed_above: std::collections::HashMap<i32, Vec<i32>>,
83	}
84	
85	/// The wire columns one merge measure's partial state occupies on the exchange row.
86	///
87	/// `position` indexes the row the *FE* declared (one column per intermediate slot); the extra
88	/// types of a wider state are inserted behind it, which is where the partial fragment emitted
89	/// them.

164	impl TranslatePlan for TPlan {
165	    /// Translates a flat preorder StarRocks plan into a Substrait relation tree.
166	    fn translate(&self, ctx: &mut PlanContext<'_>) -> Result<TranslatedRel> {
167	        if self.nodes.is_empty() {
168	            return Err(TranslateError::malformed("TPlan.nodes is empty"));
169	        }
170	        let mut cursor = PlanNodeCursor::new(&self.nodes);

185	impl<'a> PlanNodeCursor<'a> {
186	    /// Creates a cursor at the start of a plan node list.
187	    fn new(nodes: &'a [TPlanNode]) -> Self {
188	        Self { nodes, idx: 0 }
189	    }
190	
191	    /// Translates the next preorder node and its subtree.
192	    fn translate_next(&mut self, ctx: &mut PlanContext<'_>) -> Result<TranslatedRel> {
193	        let node = self
194	            .nodes
195	            .get(self.idx)
196	            .ok_or_else(|| TranslateError::malformed("unexpected end of plan nodes"))?;
197	        self.idx += 1;
198	
199	        if node.num_children < 0 {
200	            return Err(TranslateError::malformed(format!(
201	                "node {} has negative child count {}",
202	                node.node_id, node.num_children
203	            )));
204	        }
205	
206	        let children = (0..node.num_children)
207	            .map(|_| self.translate_next(ctx))
208	            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
209	
210	        translate_plan_node(node, children, ctx)
211	    }

213	    /// Verifies that the top-level plan consumed all encoded nodes.
214	    fn ensure_consumed(&self) -> Result<()> {
215	        if self.idx != self.nodes.len() {
216	            return Err(TranslateError::malformed(format!(
217	                "TPlan had {} trailing node(s)",
218	                self.nodes.len() - self.idx
219	            )));

229	    children: Vec<TranslatedRel>,
230	    ctx: &mut PlanContext<'_>,

232	    let translated = match node.node_type {

243	            node_id: node.node_id,
244	            node_type: node.node_type,

251	/// Wraps a relation in a Substrait fetch when the StarRocks node carries a limit or offset.
252	///
253	/// `TPlanNode::limit` applies to any node type; a skip offset only appears on sort and exchange
254	/// payloads.
255	// The deprecated plain offset/count oneof variants share wire tags with their expression
256	// counterparts and are the fields DuckDB's Substrait consumer reads.
257	#[allow(deprecated)]
258	fn apply_fetch(input: TranslatedRel, node: &TPlanNode) -> TranslatedRel {
259	    let offset = node
260	        .sort_node
261	        .as_ref()
262	        .and_then(|sort| sort.offset)
263	        .or_else(|| {
264	            node.exchange_node
265	                .as_ref()
266	                .and_then(|exchange| exchange.offset)
267	        })
268	        .unwrap_or(0);
269	    if node.limit < 0 && offset == 0 {
270	        return input;
271	    }
272	    let TranslatedRel {
273	        rel,
274	        row_tuples,
275	        output_width,
276	        carried_slots,
277	    } = input;
278	    // For an offset-only fetch, emit an explicit unlimited count: the consumer reads the plain
279	    // count field without checking the oneof, and an unset count would decode as `LIMIT 0`.
280	    let count = if node.limit >= 0 { node.limit } else { -1 };
281	    let count_mode = Some(fetch_rel::CountMode::Count(count));
282	    let offset_mode = (offset != 0).then_some(fetch_rel::OffsetMode::Offset(offset));
283	    TranslatedRel {
284	        rel: Rel {
285	            rel_type: Some(rel::RelType::Fetch(Box::new(FetchRel {
286	                input: Some(Box::new(rel)),
287	                offset_mode,
288	                count_mode,
289	                ..Default::default()
290	            }))),
291	        },
292	        row_tuples,
293	        output_width,
294	        // A fetch keeps the row layout, carried columns included.
295	        carried_slots,
296	    }
297	}

273	6. **q11 returns 0 rows on both engines** because the bench kit does not scale the 0.0001 fraction; the compare cannot confirm correctness of q11 at SF1000.
274	7. **cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of leaked parked output in the pool** (B4). Re-run on a clean CN before quoting them; the reservation-gate blocks in C3 depend on that leak.
275	8. **Sample size.** Warm medians are n=2; cn4 q02 has a 21% spread (1264 vs 1044 ms) that tracks one partsupp scan fragment; the six failures and their standalone counterparts ran once each.
276	9. **Can the engine run two fragments concurrently on one `SiriusContext`?** The single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` and shared `task_creator_` say no today; the cost of lifting that (needed for streaming receivers, B1 route 2) was not scoped.
277	10. **Host spill throughput.** B2's "five of six would pass" assumes a working spill at 279 GB GPU+HOST; no spill bandwidth was measured, and q09 is marginal.
278	11. **`enable_single_node_schedule` with FILES()** qualifies by code reading (`JobSpec.supportSingleNodeParallelSchedule`, `ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode`) but was not exercised.
279	12. **The receive-side unpack at 2.1 TB/s vs the pack at 63 GB/s** points at the 8 MiB `chunked_pack` (B5) but no alternative pack was timed.
280	13. **Standalone q11 scans partsupp once** (Quent shows one 16.4 GB GPU_SCAN for two CTE_SCANs) while the plan shows a CTE with two consumers; how the second consumer is served was not pursued.
281	14. **Session cold start.** cn1 q01 cold 9359 ms vs 5073 warm: the first fragment's summed `GPU_SCAN` was 25.9 s vs 12.2 s (cn1-quent.txt q01.r0 / r1), i.e. the very first GPU scan of the CN process runs ~2x slower per split; standalone's first query shows a smaller version (Comp 23.0 vs 19.0 s). Not separated into GPFS/O_DIRECT first-touch, CUDA module load, or pool warm-up.
282	15. **Standalone warm-run spread.** standalone q03 2479/3622 ms and q04 2113/1678 ms (runs.csv); the slow q03 run is a slow scan (standalone-quent.txt lines 43-54: `GPU_SCAN(10)` 11.24 s vs 7.20 s summed). With n=2 the q03/q04 1-CN parity ratios (1.02/0.98) are not distinguishable from 1.1-1.25. Re-run with n>=5 before quoting parity for these two.
283	16. **Join-fragment over-reservation.** q04 F00 253 GB requested for 61 GB peak, q07 F08 163 GB for 26 GB (C3). The hash-join / partition / concat reservation estimates were not read; whether they use a no-history multiplier like the scan's 8x is unknown.
284	17. **q16 workaround.** `SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1` is only the CN's error-text suggestion; not run. q16 also has the same partsupp-broadcast (exch 2) and `NULL AWARE LEFT ANTI JOIN (BROADCAST)` on supplier (exch 7) shape as the other WITH queries (survey/plan-summary.txt line 32), so it will inherit P2/P5 once it translates.
285	18. **Shuffle skew at 4 CNs** (P3): q07 exch 20 2.7x, q02 exch 31 one empty CN, q11 exch 4 2.7x, all on low-NDV nation/region keys. No wall-clock loss was attributable at these volumes; not measured for a shuffle where the skewed stream is the large one.

186	struct ServiceCore {
187	    /// Reusable StarRocks thrift-to-Substrait fragment translator.
188	    translator: PlanTranslator,
189	    /// Executes a translated fragment into Arrow result batches. Production injects the GPU-backed
190	    /// `SiriusEngine` (via [`SiriusComputeNodeService::with_executor`]); tests use a stub.
191	    executor: Arc<dyn FragmentExecutor>,
192	    /// Buffers executed-fragment results for FE `fetch_data` collection.
193	    results: ResultStore,
194	    /// Sequential same-node fragment exchange state.
195	    exchanges: LocalExchange,
196	    /// StarRocks may send a descriptor table once per query and mark later fragments as cached.
197	    descriptor_tables: Mutex<HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, TDescriptorTable>>,
198	    /// The exchange endpoint this CN advertises; destinations matching it are local.
199	    identity: ExchangeIdentity,
200	    /// The nixl transport tier for remote destinations. `None` keeps every remote destination a
201	    /// loud error naming how to enable it.
202	    transport: Option<NixlTransport>,
203	    /// Staging arena `(base, capacity)`, cached after the first lookup (the arena never moves).
204	    /// The executor serves every staging call from a thread-safe arena handle, never from the
205	    /// engine's request queue, so a lease request costs a mutex — not an engine wait.
206	    staging_info: Mutex<Option<(u64, u64)>>,
207	    /// Whether sender-only fragments are queued on the dispatch worker instead of running inside
208	    /// their exec_plan_fragment RPC. Off unless `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH` is set at
209	    /// bring-up (or a test flips it); see [`SiriusComputeNodeService::try_dispatch_sender`].
210	    async_sender_dispatch: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
211	}
212	
213	impl SiriusComputeNodeService {
214	    /// Test-only constructor with the placeholder [`StubExecutor`] and the default local
215	    /// identity. Production injects everything via [`with_transport`](Self::with_transport).
216	    #[cfg(test)]
217	    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
218	        Self::with_executor(
219	            Arc::new(StubExecutor),
220	            ExchangeIdentity::new("127.0.0.1", 8060),
221	        )
222	    }
223	
224	    /// [`with_transport`](Self::with_transport) without a nixl transport: every remote
225	    /// destination stays a loud error.
226	    #[cfg(test)]
227	    pub(crate) fn with_executor(
228	        executor: Arc<dyn FragmentExecutor>,
229	        identity: ExchangeIdentity,
230	    ) -> Self {
231	        Self::with_transport(executor, identity, None)
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Builds the service with a caller-provided fragment executor (e.g. the GPU-backed
235	    /// `SiriusEngine`), this CN's advertised exchange identity, and an optional nixl transport
236	    /// for remote destinations, shared across BRPC connections via the `Arc`. Also spawns the
237	    /// fragment dispatch worker.
238	    pub(crate) fn with_transport(
239	        executor: Arc<dyn FragmentExecutor>,
240	        identity: ExchangeIdentity,
241	        transport: Option<NixlTransport>,
242	    ) -> Self {
243	        let core = Arc::new(ServiceCore {
244	            translator: PlanTranslator::new(),
245	            executor,
246	            results: ResultStore::default(),
247	            exchanges: LocalExchange::default(),
248	            descriptor_tables: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
249	            identity,
250	            transport,
251	            staging_info: Mutex::new(None),
252	            async_sender_dispatch: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(
253	                Self::async_sender_dispatch_from_env(),
254	            ),
255	        });
256	        // A dedicated thread with a std channel (not a tokio task): fragment execution is
257	        // synchronous and blocking, so it gets the same dedicated-thread shape as the engine
258	        // itself, and the BRPC current-thread runtime is never involved.
259	        let (ready_fragments, worker_inbox) = mpsc::channel();
260	        let worker_core = Arc::clone(&core);
261	        std::thread::Builder::new()
262	            .name("fragment-dispatch".to_string())
263	            .spawn(move || dispatch_worker(worker_core, worker_inbox))
264	            .expect("failed to spawn fragment dispatch worker");
265	        Self {
266	            core,
267	            ready_fragments,
268	        }
269	    }

# Fragments

A **fragment** is one runnable piece of a (possibly multi-node) query: a bound plan, its declared
input/output streams, and the machinery to build, run, and drain it. [Streaming
Sessions](streaming-sessions.md) covers the low-level primitives a fragment is built on
(`exec::batch_stream`, `STREAMING_SOURCE`/`STREAMING_SINK`, the id-addressed `exec::stream_session`
router). This document covers the layer above: how a Substrait or DuckDB plan becomes a fragment,
how its declared streams get a schema before the plan is even bound, and how multiple fragments —
possibly owned by different processes — chain together via `relay_from()`.

Two classes do this, at two different layers:

| | `exec::streaming_fragment` | `sirius::ffi::Fragment` |
|---|---|---|
| **Files** | `src/include/exec/streaming_fragment.hpp`, `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp` | `src/include/sirius_ffi.hpp`, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp` |
| **Caller** | C++ code already inside a live `duckdb::ClientContext` and transaction (e.g. the transparent path, `Context::execute_substrait`) | Any caller that must not include DuckDB/cuDF headers — the Rust bindings, or a standalone C++ embedder |
| **Owns the connection?** | No — borrows the caller's `ClientContext` | Yes — brings up its own embedded `duckdb::DuckDB` + `Connection` (`Context`) |
| **Transaction / query window** | Caller's responsibility to bracket | Manages its own, internally, across two phases (see below) |
| **Shape** | One output-only or gather sink; `spec.plan_source` is a `LogicalOperator` factory | Declare → build → relay → run, addressable by stream id from outside the process |

`sirius::ffi::Fragment` is a PIMPL wrapper around exactly one `exec::streaming_fragment` (or, for a
result fragment, around the single-shot `sirius_interface` path) — it exists to give a
cross-language caller everything `streaming_fragment` needs (a connection, a transaction, a query
window, a bind catalog) without exposing any of it.

## Quick path

```cpp
// exec::streaming_fragment — caller already owns the transaction/window.
fragment_spec spec;
spec.plan_source = my_plan_source;     // ClientContext& -> LogicalOperator
spec.outputs     = {0};                // one output stream
streaming_fragment frag(client, std::move(spec));
frag.build(query_id);
frag.run();                            // blocks
drain(frag.session(), 0);              // pull() until drained
```

```cpp
// sirius::ffi::Fragment — cross-language, owns everything.
auto ctx = make_context();
auto sender = make_fragment(*ctx);
sender->declare_output(0);
sender->build(substrait_plan_bytes);   // opens + closes its own setup transaction
sender->run();                         // blocks; closes the query lifecycle

auto receiver = make_fragment(*ctx);
receiver->declare_input_column(0, "a", "BIGINT");
receiver->build(other_plan_bytes);     // this plan reads sirius_stream_source(0) / view sirius_stream_0
receiver->relay_from(*sender, /*source_stream_id=*/0, /*input_stream_id=*/0, /*sender_id=*/0);
receiver->run();
```

## `stream_bind_catalog` + `sirius_stream_source` — bridging bind time and plan time

**Files:** `src/include/exec/stream_bind_catalog.hpp`, `src/exec/stream_bind_catalog.cpp`,
`src/include/exec/stream_plan_bindings.hpp`, `src/exec/stream_plan_bindings.cpp`

A fragment's input streams do not exist as DuckDB tables — there is nothing in the catalog for the
binder to look up. `sirius_stream_source(id)`, a table function, stands in for one: its **bind**
resolves a declared stream's schema (names + types) so the binder is satisfied; its **body never
runs** — the physical plan generator replaces every `sirius_stream_source` scan with a
`STREAMING_SOURCE` operator before execution. A plan does not call the function directly; it reads
`CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW main.sirius_stream_<id> AS SELECT * FROM sirius_stream_source(<id>)`, so a
Substrait or SQL plan sees an ordinary-looking view name (`stream_view_name(id)` gives callers that
exact string).

Bind time and plan time are far apart — DuckDB binds a table function long before physical planning
runs — so both sides need a shared place to look up a declared stream's schema. That place is
`stream_bind_catalog`, a `duckdb::ClientContextState` registered per-connection:

```cpp
class stream_bind_catalog : public duckdb::ClientContextState {
 public:
  static constexpr const char* kStateKey = "sirius_stream_catalog";

  void declare(stream_id_t id, stream_input_binding binding);  // overwrites same-id entry
  void clear();                                                 // drop every declaration
  void erase(stream_id_t id);                                   // drop one; no-op if absent

1	//! Phase classification for StarRocks aggregation nodes.
     2	//!
     3	//! StarRocks encodes the phase of a (possibly multi-phase) aggregation in two thrift fields:
     4	//! `TAggregationNode.need_finalize` (does this node produce final values?) and, per measure,
     5	//! `TAggregateExpr.is_merge_agg` (does this measure consume partial states?). The combinations
     6	//! map onto the FE's phase names:
     7	//!
     8	//! | `need_finalize` | `is_merge_agg` | FE phase          | classification          |
     9	//! |-----------------|----------------|-------------------|-------------------------|
    10	//! | true            | none           | one-phase         | [`AggPhase::OneShot`]   |
    11	//! | false           | none           | update serialize  | [`AggPhase::Partial`]   |
    12	//! | true            | all            | merge finalize    | [`AggPhase::Merge`]     |
    13	//! | false           | all            | merge serialize   | error (3/4-phase plan)  |
    14	//! | —               | mixed          | —                 | error                   |
    15	//!
    16	//! Both legacy guards — the node-level `need_finalize` check and the expression-level
    17	//! `is_merge_agg` rejection — are subsumed here. They must never be relaxed independently: the
    18	//! node-level tuple-id check alone does not stop a merge node (new-optimizer plans always set
    19	//! `intermediate_tuple_id == output_tuple_id`), so a classifier that saw only `need_finalize`
    20	//! would translate a merge node as a one-shot aggregate and double-aggregate silently.
    21	
    22	use starrocks_thrift::plan_nodes::{TAggregationNode, TPlanNodeType};
    23	
    24	use crate::error::{Result, TranslateError};
    25	
    26	/// The role an aggregation node plays in the FE's aggregation plan.
    27	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    28	pub(crate) enum AggPhase {
    29	    /// One-phase finalized aggregation over raw rows (`new_planner_agg_stage = 1` plans).
    30	    OneShot,
    31	    /// First phase of a two-phase plan ("update serialize"): aggregates raw rows and emits
    32	    /// partial-state columns without finalizing.
    33	    Partial,
    34	    /// Final phase of a two-phase plan ("merge finalize"): merges partial states arriving
    35	    /// from an exchange and finalizes.
    36	    Merge,
    37	}
    38	
    39	/// Classifies an aggregation node's phase from `need_finalize` and the measures'
    40	/// `is_merge_agg` flags.
    41	///
    42	/// A measure whose root expression carries no `agg_expr` counts as non-merge here; the
    43	/// expression translator rejects such a measure with its own malformed-aggregate error.
    44	pub(crate) fn classify(
    45	    node_id: i32,
    46	    node_type: TPlanNodeType,
    47	    agg: &TAggregationNode,
    48	) -> Result<AggPhase> {
    49	    let merge_flags = agg.aggregate_functions.iter().map(|expr| {
    50	        expr.nodes
    51	            .first()
    52	            .and_then(|root| root.agg_expr.as_ref())
    53	            .is_some_and(|agg_expr| agg_expr.is_merge_agg)
    54	    });
    55	    let (mut merge, mut update) = (0usize, 0usize);
    56	    for is_merge in merge_flags {
    57	        if is_merge {
    58	            merge += 1;
    59	        } else {
    60	            update += 1;
    61	        }
    62	    }
    63	    match (agg.need_finalize, merge, update) {
    64	        (true, 0, _) => Ok(AggPhase::OneShot),
    65	        (false, 0, _) => Ok(AggPhase::Partial),
    66	        (true, _, 0) => Ok(AggPhase::Merge),
    67	        (false, _, 0) => Err(TranslateError::UnsupportedPlanNode {
    68	            node_id,
    69	            node_type,
    70	            reason: "merge-serialize aggregation (a 3/4-phase DISTINCT plan) is not supported \
    71	                     (SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1)",
    72	        }),
    73	        _ => Err(TranslateError::UnsupportedPlanNode {
    74	            node_id,
    75	            node_type,
    76	            reason: "aggregation node mixes merge and update aggregate functions \
    77	                     (SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1)",
    78	        }),
    79	    }
    80	}

# CN tunables

Environment variables the Sirius StarRocks CN reads. Most operators only need a
worked config (`configs/gb200-4gpu/engine-a.env`, or the launcher in
`bench/rtxpro6000-2gpu/`) and should not set these by hand.

## How they work

Transport knobs live in one registry, [`src/tunable.rs`](../src/tunable.rs).
They are resolved once at bring-up: a typo or out-of-range value **fails CN
startup** (it is never clamped or silently ignored). The CN then logs the
resolved set — that line is what the process actually got, not what the
launcher echoed.

Unset means the compiled default. Empty string is treated as unset.

Everything else below is read outside that registry and follows its own rules.

## Transport (validated registry)

| Knob | Role |
|---|---|
| `SIRIUS_CN_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECS` | How long a CN waits for a peer RPC (lease, metadata). Raise this before treating a large-SF timeout as a query bug — a busy peer can sit behind this bound. |
| `SIRIUS_CN_NIXL_XFER_TIMEOUT_SECS` | How long one nixl WRITE may take. Distinguishes a stuck fabric from a busy peer. |
| `SIRIUS_CN_NIXL_CANARY_BYTES` / `_FLOOR_GBPS` | First-contact bandwidth probe. A slow link is refused so a silent staged-copy fallback cannot look like a healthy transfer. `0` on the floor disables the check. |
| `SIRIUS_CN_NIXL_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_SECS` / `_EXPECT_PEERS` | Bring-up session warmup. The timeout is a budget, not a hard fail; expect-peers ends the loop early once that many peers are up. |

Related, but not in the registry: `SIRIUS_CN_NIXL_WARMUP` (off switch) and
`SIRIUS_CN_NIXL_WARMUP_PEERS` (explicit peer list).

## Exchange staging

`SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES` sizes each CN's GPU staging arena. Unset means
**no arena**: the CN boots and serves local work, then every remote exchange
fails. There is no engine default — launchers pick a size per box.

## Engine-side
